metadata.title: [CHORE]: Document cargo-vet workflow for Rust dependency updates
metadata.author: lucarlig

description:
### 🔧 Chore Summary

Document the expected `cargo-vet` workflow for Rust dependency updates in the ContextForge release management guide, and decide how the same process should be handled for the `cpex-plugins` repo.

Recent release-prep CI failed in the Rust `Supply-chain vet` job because `make rust-vet` runs `cargo vet check` and dependency updates introduced unvetted crate versions.

---

### 🧱 Area Affected

Choose the general area(s) that this chore affects:

- [x] GitHub Actions / CI Pipelines
- [ ] Pre-commit hooks / linters
- [ ] Formatting (black, isort, ruff, etc.)
- [ ] Type-checking (mypy, pyright, pytype, etc.)
- [x] Dependency cleanup or updates
- [x] Build system or `Makefile`
- [ ] Containerization (Docker/Podman)
- [x] Docs or spellcheck
- [x] SBOM, CVE scans, licenses, or security checks
- [x] Other: Rust supply-chain audit process

---

### ⚙️ Context / Rationale

ContextForge currently has a strict Rust supply-chain check:

- `make rust-vet` installs `cargo-vet` if needed and runs `cargo vet check`
- `.github/workflows/rust.yml` runs this in the `Supply-chain vet` job
- release wheel/sdist jobs depend on `supply-chain-vet`
- `supply-chain/config.toml` imports third-party audit sets, including Bytecode Alliance, Google, Mozilla, and others

A recent CI failure showed:

- `24 unvetted dependencies`
- missing `safe-to-deploy`
- recommended `cargo vet diff` / `cargo vet inspect` commands
- estimated audit backlog: `132733 lines`

Failure reference:
https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/actions/runs/25192951655/job/73867027284#step:5:77

Relevant Makefile target:
https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/blob/main/Makefile#L8691-L8695

Cargo-vet docs:
https://mozilla.github.io/cargo-vet/

The release process should explain what maintainers are expected to do before release time when Rust dependencies are updated, instead of discovering this only when release CI fails.

---

### 📦 Related Make Targets

- `make rust-vet` - run `cargo vet check` against the Rust workspace supply-chain policy
- `make rust-deny` - run cargo-deny policy checks
- `make rust-licenses` - run Rust license checks
- `make rust-build` / `make rust-test` - validate Rust workspace after dependency changes

---

### 📋 Acceptance Criteria

Define what "done" looks like for this task.

- [ ] Update `docs/docs/development/release-management.md` section 3, or nearby release dependency section, with a Cargo Vet subsection.
- [ ] Document when to run `make rust-vet`, especially after `cargo update` or Rust dependency changes.
- [ ] Document how to resolve failures:
  - run the suggested `cargo vet diff <crate> <old> <new>` for version deltas
  - run `cargo vet inspect <crate> <version>` for new crates
  - record completed audits with `cargo vet certify`
  - update `supply-chain/audits.toml` and/or `supply-chain/config.toml` as appropriate
- [ ] Document who may perform/approve audits, for example Rust maintainers or security reviewers familiar with the affected crate and `safe-to-deploy` criteria.
- [ ] Document when exemptions are acceptable, and that frequent exemptions reduce the value of the supply-chain gate.
- [ ] Document that large/high-risk diffs should be planned before release freeze, not handled ad hoc during release tagging.
- [ ] Clarify whether `cargo-vet` is intended to be blocking for release CI, advisory only, or blocking only after a maturity date.
- [ ] Check the `cpex-plugins` repo and either add equivalent documentation there or open a companion issue for the same policy.
- [ ] Verify the documented flow against current `supply-chain/config.toml`, `supply-chain/audits.toml`, and `.github/workflows/rust.yml`.

---

### 🧩 Additional Context

Cargo-vet is intended to ensure Rust third-party dependencies have been audited by trusted entities or by project maintainers. It can reuse audits from trusted sources and can audit only version diffs where possible, but new crates or large version jumps may require substantial manual review.

This issue is only for documenting and deciding the workflow. It should not silently remove `cargo-vet` or weaken the CI gate unless maintainers explicitly decide that is the desired policy.
